newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria sets up poll watchdog committee.
newsitem.headline: Algeria sets up poll watchdog committee.

text.p: Algerian President Liamine Zeroual on Thursday signed a decree setting up a committee to supervise parliamentary elections on June 5, the official Algerian news agency APS said.

Signing into law of the National Independent Committee for Supervision of the Legislative Elections marked the end of a series of talks between Zeroual and political parties competing for the poll, APS said. The talks were held from late February until Wednesday.
Algeria has been without an elected parliament and elected local councils since 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
Scrapping the election plunged Algeria into violence, pitting Moslem guerrillas against government forces, during which about 60,000 people have died.

Algeria, striving to allay politicians' suspicions over the fairness of the poll, has invited observers from the United Nations, the Organisation of African Unity and the Arab League to monitor the elections.
Officials from the three groups will arrive late on Thursday in Algiers to hold talks with the authorities on their mission.
